name: Misfits and Hooligans
description: At 5:49 — five minutes and forty-nine seconds — "Misfits and Hooligans" is That Boy Hi Hat's longest record on Spotify, and it earns every second. An Idol or Icon standout from 2021, the track is a sprawling statement of alternative rap built for the outsiders, and it sounds like a manifesto written for kids who never fit the room. In the vein of the great underground crew records of the alt rap era, the production is defiant by design: a hard-hitting drum pattern drives the beat from the first bar, an 808 bass rolls underneath the whole arrangement, and claps crack in the chorus like a crowd finding its rhythm. Snare hits land with aggressive snap throughout, hi-hats stay crisp and busy, and ad-libs pile up layered underneath the hook until the whole mix feels like a room full of people. For fans of anthemic post trap, dark trap, and futuristic rap, the record plays like a set-closer: raw, energetic, and rebellious in the best way. That Boy Hi Hat writes verses that stack into verses, the beat breathes, and the triumphant energy compounds rather than dissipates — a hype record about belonging that recalls the collectivist spirit of the early underground hip hop movement. The minor-key grit never tips into major-key sweetness; the tones stay heavy and the textures stay thick, with real depth in the low end. It sits in the catalog as the communal counterweight to the lonelier cuts, and the current wave of cinematic rap rarely gets this physical. In a scene that rewards isolation, "Misfits and Hooligans" is That Boy Hi Hat choosing the crowd — gritty, rebellious, and built to be shouted back, with a studio-polished low end under the raw drums.
